rationale: Second UE-triggered Service Request after AN-release/UP deactivation leaves UL user plane dead; trigger is ordinary CM-IDLE/Service Request cycling, no NF or peer restart/failure event.

AMF treats GUTI from an unconfirmed Registration Accept as unknown after UE context release/reconnect; spec-conformance NAS procedure bug, the UE context release is a normal procedure, not a peer failure.

Spoofed PFCP Association Setup/Update (forged Node ID, newer Recovery Time Stamp, SARR) makes SMF release all sessions; adversarial-input/authentication defect with no real peer failure (fixed by source-IP validation).
Question whether PFCP 'REMOTE Holding Timeout' debug logs are normal; maintainer confirms normal behaviour.
PDU session not established with 'Duplicated PDU session ID' on old free5gc v3.1.1 k8s deployment; no NF/peer failure event, maintainer only suggests upgrading; usage/unresolved.
AMF UE-connectivity metric counter decrements below zero on each inactivity/idle transition; metrics bug on normal idle path, no failure event.

UPF PFCP agent does not reset its heartbeat timer when it receives SMF heartbeats, so the association is shut down spuriously; this is a heartbeat/association-handling bug, but there is no real peer failure (failure detection itself misfires), so condition (1) is unclear.

upg-vpp UPF suddenly loses UE contexts and drops the PFCP association; SMF never re-associates and keeps sending Session Establishment, which is answered 'No established PFCP Association', so all PDU sessions are rejected until SMF restart (observable, persistent).

After SMF restart and re-association the UPF overwrites the association but keeps all old PFCP sessions; the restarted SMF reuses CP SEIDs from 1, so new sessions collide with kept ones and are rejected (UE gets PDU Session Establishment Reject #38) and the orphaned sessions are never deleted.

When PFCP establishment fails (UPF associated but unresponsive) and/or the AMF is unreachable for N1N2MessageTransfer after the 201, SMF early-returns without RemoveSMContext, leaking SMContexts, UE IPs and TEIDs (31 requests leak 31); only WARN logs about the failed transfer, slow leak not visible to a short test. Thread: reject side already fixed in #236, accept side still open.
Open5GS SMF never completes PFCP association with ONF UPF (response not received by SMF stack); initial interop/network setup problem, no restart/failure event.

SMF fatal error (Invalid Downlink Data Service Information) when a UE reconnects after UE context release; normal-path crash fixed in v2.3.0, not triggered by an NF/peer failure (the SMF restart afterwards is a consequence).

After UPF restart, SMF PFCP restoration re-installs sessions with pre-outage UE IPs while UEs re-registered with new IPs, so downlink PDRs are keyed on stale IPs and DL traffic is silently dropped with no error/counter. Thread: needs release still in flight at restoration; reproducible deterministically, and the UE data plane stays down when probed.

AMF NGAP worker goroutines die permanently after handler panics triggered by a malicious Handover nil-deref PoC, eventually blocking NGSetup; adversarial-input/fuzzing trigger and internal worker-pool robustness, no NF/peer failure event.

Forged unauthenticated PFCP Association Setup with the SMF's Node ID makes the UPF delete the real association and its sessions, plus unbounded peer-table growth from distinct Node IDs; adversarial spoofing/DoS, no real peer failure.

NRF segfaults when an NF (AUSF) that has a subscription for its type is de-registered via DELETE nf-instance; concerns NRF registration/subscription state on NF departure, but it is a graceful deregistration rather than a crash/heartbeat-loss, so the failure-event criterion is ambiguous.
Open5GS services hang and eNBs go out of service until manual restart; only an S1AP encode failure seen, no identified restart/peer-failure trigger, unresolved and auto-closed.

When a gNB with 40+ UEs disconnects (N2/SCTP loss), the AMF's mass cleanup of the gNB's UEs exhausts the SBI socket pool and aborts on Assertion 'sockinfo'; root cause is undersized memory pool during peer-failure cleanup (thread: fixed by enlarging the pool), so 'other'.
AMF crashes after UE release/airplane mode; thread shows it is triggered by NEA1 ciphering configuration (NAS security bug), not a peer failure.
UPF returns Accepted when Session Modification RemovePDR references a non-existent PDR; crafted-input PFCP handling bug, no restart/peer failure.

SMF-UPF PFCP association flaps/never stabilises in a split-VM setup; thread: caused by getnameinfo() reverse-DNS timeout (10 s) in the environment, changed in code but not a restart/peer-failure state bug.

Thread: after one of two UPFs is killed and SMF enters association retry, SMF round-robin still assigns new sessions to the dead UPF because selection does not check that the PFCP association is still active; failures are logged and a retry lands on the live UPF, so not persistent.
MME locks up and all UEs go offline until service restart; trigger unknown (maintainer suspects MME infinite loop), no identified NF/peer failure event; auto-closed.
All UEs go down intermittently with SGW GTP send failures (EAGAIN) and suspected MME infinite loop; no restart/peer-failure trigger identified, auto-closed.

After UPF heartbeat timeout the SMF never releases existing sessions (4G path; thread: 5G released only via reselect_upf), keeping them active and accounting while the UPF is gone until it returns and restoration runs; heartbeat give-up is logged and the UE outage is inherent to the UPF being down, so a crash/persistent-failure oracle would not flag it.

UPF kept sending DL GTP to the first gNB after a detach and re-attach, idle/Service Request or handover. That is a normal mobility/re-attach path with no NF/peer failure; the restart was only the workaround. Thread: fixed by a later release.

Starts from an Error Indication for the IMS default bearer (a peer lost-state signal), followed by Delete Bearer Request and a Cause-only failure response from the MME. SGW-C removes only the default bearer and leaves an empty sgwc_sess_t; a later Release Access Bearers Request hits ogs_assert and aborts SGW-C.

Second registration after a normal deregistration fails (AMF log ends and the daemon restarts); restarting NRF and AMF works around it. The trigger is a normal re-registration, not an NF/peer failure, and there are no comments or root cause.
SMF assertion (policy_association_id) after an HTTP 504. Thread: the cause was a BSF missing from the deployment, required from v2.3.0, plus later NRF IPv6 config mismatches. Config/usage problem.
MME did not answer the eNB Configuration Update (unimplemented message), so the eNB restarts. Missing feature, added in the thread; not a state bug after a peer failure.

During an NRF outage (oauth GetTokenCtx fails) PCF CreateSmPolicy fails after the policy entry is inserted. It returns an error without Location, so the SMF can never delete the SM policy: an orphan entry, bounded at about 15 per UE and overwritten on reuse. The create failure is visible at that time (HTTP 500), so not silent; the effect is internal state only.
SCP returns a generic HTTP 500 instead of 502/503/504 when the target NSSF is stopped; service returns once NSSF restarts. Error-code semantics, not cross-NF state corruption or non-convergence.

Main bug: a normal-path MME crash (pkbuf/asn1c memory with large UERadioCapability). Thread: after each MME crash/restart, sessions pile up in SGW-U/UPF (715 vs about 30 at SGW-C/SMF). The maintainer confirmed PFCP has no IMSI, so duplicates cannot be reconciled after an MME (or SMF) restart. Orphan state found only by inspecting counters.

AMF reportedly reuses a TCP connection after UDM GOAWAY caused by a short idle timeout. Not a peer restart/failure, and the maintainer could not reproduce it (curl opens a new connection). Closed for inactivity.
UEs won't stay attached; SGW-C logs 'No Context' warnings. No failure/restart trigger identified and no diagnosis; the MME restart was just the user restarting services. Unresolved usage report.

Users stay connected after account expiry, core service restart and DB deletion. The restart claim could be stale state surviving restart, but there are no logs, no comments, and most of it reads as a missing subscriber-change enforcement feature.
SMF matches the PFCP Association Setup Response to the wrong UPF when FQDN NodeIDs are used (falls back to the last pool entry). Association bug at initial setup, with no failure/restart event.

Changing a registered UE's subscribed DNN leaves PDU sessions failing ('DNN Not Supported') until the core restarts. Subscription-change handling with no NF/peer failure; the restart was only the workaround.

When the UP side (SGW-U/UPF) crashes and restarts it loses all PFCP state, but SGW-C/SMF keep the old sessions. Already-attached UEs cannot send traffic and disconnects fail, and the whole CP has to be restarted to resync. The data-plane outage is persistent and visible to a UE probe.

After the N3IWUE is killed (connection-loss simulation), the N3IWF keeps the old XFRM/IPsec state, so reconnection fails ('file exists') until restart; fixed in N3IWF/UDR/n3ue. The failing party is a UE over NWu, not a listed core peer, so unclear whether it counts as a peer failure.
With the TLS config enabled, all NFs abort on getaddrinfo failure for amf.localdomain. Configuration problem.

AMF/MME do not fully clean up (orphaned UDM SDM subscription, retained MME resources) after T3550/T3450 Accept retransmissions run out because the UE never sends Complete. The trigger is UE non-response, not an NF/peer failure.

OAI SMF reuses a released session object after a normal UE deregistration and re-registration with the same PSI, leaking one UE IP per cycle. A normal-path leak; the 'restart' is just the nrUE being stopped and started cleanly.

SMF race: the UDM deregistration of a released session is cancelled when an unrelated HTTP/2 stream with the same pool id closes, leaving the session stuck in will_deregister. Normal-path transaction/stream id confusion, no failure event.

NFs crash after about 48h idle. Thread: double free when the NRF subscription validity timer fires for the second time; fixed in v2.5.6. Timer/lifecycle crash in normal operation, not after an NF/peer failure.
Adversarial DoS: repeated unauthenticated SCTP associations push the AMF socket fd past FD_SETSIZE and cause an FD_SET overflow abort. Attack-input territory with no NF/peer failure.
NRF crashes on NFRegister bodies containing nfSetRecoveryTimeList/serviceSetRecoveryTimeList (found by extremal schema testing). Input-handling crash with no peer failure.

gNB sends NG Reset (peer lost-state signal) in response to a UE Context Release Command; AMF's handling of the reset against the pending UE context release hits a fatal error and the AMF crashes. Fixed in main per maintainer.

Users stay connected after deletion from HSS and after an unspecified 'service restart'; mostly a request that subscriber deletion should detach UEs (feature-like), and which service was restarted / whether stale sessions survive a core NF restart is unclear; no comments.

Second SMF in another container logs 'No heartbeat' from NRF after UDM discovery, then keeps de-/re-registering with NRF (inconsistent SMF/NRF state). Heartbeat loss is present but the thread is a 'what am I misconfiguring' question with no resolution; code bug vs config unclear.
HSS reports 'Cannot find IMSI in DB' and UEs cannot attach; thread: the MongoDB service had failed. Database outage, not an NF/peer failure with cross-NF state; restarting HSS is just the workaround.

Thread: eNB sends GTP-U Error Indication during Delete Bearer procedure; the resulting DDN makes MME overwrite bearer->xact, so the Delete Bearer Response carries a wrong sequence number and SGW-C crashes. Root cause is a transaction-context overwrite on Error Indication handling (other).
Static UE IP cannot be removed/changed; restarting services mentioned only in passing and reinstalling v1.2.4 fixed it. Not a restart/peer-failure bug.

Long production thread of many MME/SGW-U assertions under load (timer pool, missing bearer/sess, paging, memory pools, PDN type 0) fixed across releases; these are normal-path/resource crashes, and eNB SCTP COMM_LOST over satellite was explained as expected UE cleanup, not a state bug.

GTP-U peer nodes for old eNB S1-U addresses are never reclaimed, so eNB renumbering exhausts the gtp_node pool and attaches fail. Cross-NF peer state leak, but the trigger is eNB address renumbering/reconfiguration rather than a restart/failure event, so inclusion is ambiguous.

After SMF is killed and UPF's PFCP heartbeat gives up, UPF only returns to will_associate and keeps all sessions of that SMF (deleted only if SMF returns with new Recovery Time Stamp), contrary to TS 23.527. Leftover sessions are internal state with no error, so not visible to a crash/persistent-failure oracle.
No downlink traffic with multiple eNBs; thread: config was fine and the problem disappeared with a different UE model (3GPP release mismatch). UE/usage issue, no failure event.
UPF fails to start because GTP-U bind address already in use; configuration/usage question.

Shutting down the host running UPFs causes PFCP heartbeat loss; SMF's N4 no-heartbeat cleanup loop (reused 'next' iterator and already-freed node pointer, session without sm_context_ref) hits an assertion and SMF crashes. Thread: maintainer fixed both issues.
UE gets security mode reject after EPC runs for some time; restarting EPC is only the workaround and the cause (fixed via #214) is not a peer failure/restart.

AMF loses NRF heartbeat and repeatedly re-registers; thread: each re-registration cycle created duplicate NF-status subscriptions and stale subscription_data was not cleaned on non-204 DELETE, exhausting the pool until AMF asserts in ogs_sbi_subscription_data_add. Crash is visible, but it took hours of re-registration cycles, so a short test would not see it.

When SMF is unreachable (Session Report Responses dropped via iptables), UPF never frees the PfcpXact for PFCP Session Report, leaking transactions until pfcpXactPool is empty; afterwards new PFCP procedures (Service Request modification) keep failing. Leak itself raises no error until exhaustion; the reproducer exhausts it within one test.
NRF does not return a default heartbeatTimer when NF omits it in registration; spec-compliance/feature fix, not triggered by a failure/restart.
UE released ~5 s after registration because first registration uses DNN ims / user-plane config issue; no peer failure event.

After killing and restarting gNB CU/DU (SCTP shutdown, new NGSetup), SMF's previously allocated UE IP is not released, so SMF reports 'IP is used' / 'UE IP pool exhausted' and PDU session establishment is not accepted until free5GC is restarted. Intermittent but persistent once hit.
Multi-UPF ULCL topology shows PFCP retransmits and 'Index Pool is full'; thread: config indentation errors and outdated test configs, passes on updated version. Config issue, no failure event.
UPF and SMF crash on start in Kubernetes on Alpine; thread: stack overflow on musl/Alpine, fixed. Normal-path platform crash, not a restart/peer-failure bug.

On every SMF restart a DB-persisted monotonic smfCount is incremented and used as a 5000-address stride, so after one restart (on a /24) SMF hands out UE IPs outside the configured pool; session comes up and uplink works but downlink is dead. Restart-count misused as instance index with no pool bound check (other); silent, and a ping probe would show persistent data-plane loss.

During an NRF outage, GetTokenCtx fails in SM context create and SMF returns an empty 200 without releasing the SMContext (UE IP, TEIDs), so each request leaves an SMContext the AMF has no ref to release. 'Get Token Context Error' is logged; the leak grows with no ceiling but stays internal state in a short test.

With SMF address configured in UPF, UPF sometimes stays in will_associate (rejects session establishment as 'cannot handle PFCP message') after a reboot of everything, while SMF thinks it is associated (logs show SMF requests from a different IP than the one UPF connected to). Association-handling flavour, but not reliably reproducible, not clearly after a peer restart, and possibly a k8s address config issue; no comments.
UDM returns 404 instead of 500/503 when its UE context pool (max.ue) is exhausted by >1024 SUPIs; ordinary capacity/error-code bug with no NF restart or peer failure.
PCF leaks a UeContext per unprovisioned-SUPI AM-policy create (missing UePool.Delete on UDR-404 error path); adversarial/normal-path memory leak, no peer failure event.

UPF reports PFCP Association Release Request (type 9) as not implemented when a custom SMF sends it; essentially a feature request about unimplemented message handling, no restart/peer failure; auto-closed.

MME assertion crash in nas_eps_send_esm_information_request after "S1 context has already been removed"; title "restarting" is the crash/respawn itself, thread shows no peer/eNB failure event (normal-path crash, fixed by maintainer).

N1N2MessageSubscribe stored after the HTTP thread times out (1 s), so subscriptions are orphaned; trigger is an APP-task stall that the PoC induces via an unresponsive NSSF (peer unreachability) but the reporter says any CPU/scheduling stall suffices, so it is mainly a timeout race rather than clearly a peer-failure bug.

After NRF restart the third-party NF gets 404 on heartbeat and re-registers, and NRF asserts/crashes; thread: root cause was a generic bug receiving large HTTP/2 messages, so it is unclear whether the failure is restart-specific or would hit any large registration.
"No RanUe Context" error when re-running the deregistration test without restarting the CN; thread: test harness hardcodes AMF UE NGAP ID=1, test artefact not a restart bug.
UE stops and re-attaches via eNB in another TAC but MME keeps the originally selected SGW-C; SGW selection policy/feature question, UE-only event.

Dual-EPC failover: after main EPC is brought back up and eNB re-connects, UE re-attaches but ping fails (user plane broken); restart event is clear but no replies/root cause, so unclear whether an Open5GS state bug, eNB-side stale state, or deployment misconfiguration.

SMF session count stays after gNB/UEs removed; thread: maintainer says UE contexts are intentionally kept (like idle) on gNB loss, and the bug actually fixed was a BSF binding keyed on S-NSSAI+DNN breaking normal deregistration of a 2nd UE (normal path).
AMF silently discards old NGAP UE association when a second registration for the same UE arrives, without UE Context Release; normal-path protocol handling, no NF/peer failure.
Malformed UplinkNASTransport with unknown protocol discriminator removes ran_ue but leaves amf_ue with running timers; adversarial-input bug, no peer failure.
PFCP association setup fails with DNN mismatch due to webconsole configuration order (DNN list not updated when device group added); configuration handling, no restart/peer failure.
Usage question whether Open5GS NFs are stateless; answer: state is in local memory, no reboot-safe mechanism. Not a bug report.

When UPF PFCP Session Establishment Responses are dropped (UPF unreachable on N4), SMF never releases the SM context/UE IP after PFCP timeout, so repeated failures exhaust the IP pool; thread: fix releases SM context on the reject path. Failure is logged/visible per attempt and exhaustion needs many cycles (pool shrunk to /29).

On a GTP-U Error Indication (peer lost state) the SMF/PGW-C deletes the whole IMS PDN locally without Delete Bearer Request, so MME/UE keep a ghost PDN and the UE cannot make VoLTE calls until re-attach; SMF logs ERROR at the time, and IMS service stays down.

When the PFCP session deletion fails (UPF unreachable/rejected) during local release, SMF skips CHARGING_RELEASE and leaves a zombie SMContext, so the CHF charging session is orphaned (also not released when UPF association drop sweeps contexts); only a TRACE log, internal state only.

N3IWUE reconnect after Ctrl+C fails with communicateWithUDM SYSTEM_FAILURE until UDM is restarted; the triggering event is a UE (N3IWUE) restart, not an NF/peer failure (UE-only event per codebook), and no root cause in thread.
UE context release not triggered when COTS UE goes to emergency-only / flight mode; UE-side behaviour, no NF/peer failure.
After many UEs restart some PFCP Session Establishment Requests are not handled by UPF; thread points to UPF buffer/scale limits; UE restarts, not NF/peer failure.

When gNB closes the SCTP/NGAP association before Identity Response, AMF does not free the pre-registered amf_ue, so after 1024 cycles the pool is exhausted and registrations are rejected until AMF restart; each leak is silent, and detection needs ~1024 cycles. thread: fix in amf_sbi_send_deactivate_all_ue_in_gnb.
AMF assertion in curl_multi_add_handle during shutdown after SIGTERM while fuzzed with AFLNet; shutdown/fuzzing crash, not a peer failure state bug.
NF registration via SCP to NRF gets 500 response_handler() failed; happens even on fresh start of NRF with SCP (comment), no restart-specific behaviour and no resolution; likely setup/usage issue.

NRF heartbeat timers expired for all NFs (No heartbeat, NF de-registered) and the ensuing burst of NF re-registration PUTs (plus PFCP re-association) crashed NRF with nrf_event_new assertion (event pool); thread: maintainer says fixed in v2.2.4.
SMF never deletes the PCF SM policy association on AMF-driven PDU session release; normal teardown path leak, no restart/peer failure.

Restarted SMF restarts smContextRef counter at 0, so AMF stale ref from before restart (used on UE B deregistration) releases UE A's new session; AMF gets 204 and UE A silently loses data plane. Visible only when another UE's stale ref is used after the restart (multi-UE sequence), so a standard restart test likely misses it.
upf-epc containers in restart loop due to image missing bess.ko/insmod; build/deployment issue.

After SGW restart the MME keeps old session state and sends Create Session with TEID unknown to SGW (SGW logs ASSERT !(sgw_ue)), so the UE cannot re-attach; thread: maintainer says SGW/PGW restart not supported. Process keeps running (repeated assert logs).
Custom NF heartbeat PATCH rejected with 400; thread: client sent wrong Content-Type (application/json instead of json-patch+json). Usage error.
UPF logs "Cannot find PFCP-Node" continuously after association on fresh k8s deployment; no restart/peer failure event, no resolution, likely deployment configuration.

With UE in CM_IDLE, UPF1 is killed; SMF keeps the session anchored on dead UPF1 and on Service Request just accepts/confirms activation on the crashed UPF instead of releasing/re-establishing on UPF2, so UE data plane stays down; thread: fixed via #2471 (reactivation with PDU_SESSION_ANCHOR_CHANGE).

UPF drops uplink as Source IP Spoofing (TEID/UE IP mismatch between UEs) after ~48h until services restart; thread: maintainer first blamed an SMF restart (TEID mismatch SGW-U/UPF) then found no SMF restart and fixed SGW-U sessions not deleted properly, and v2.5.0 still failed, so the failure-event link is ambiguous.
Feature request to implement Enhanced PFCP Association Release (TS 29.244 5.18); no bug or failure event.
Security report: UE-smuggled PFCP Session Establishment with a static F-TEID colliding with a live TEID is accepted; adversarial input explicitly outside the restoration path, no peer failure.

After gNB restart forces re-registration while AMF holds the NG context, t_ng_holding expiry removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF/UPF session, so DL FAR keeps pointing at a dead gNB TEID and the UE is blackholed with no paging and no error; reporter says it persists until the UE re-registers (getting a new IP since the old session still holds it).

Killing the RAN simulator (SCTP drop) makes AMF send a burst of SM-context updates; thread: reporter's debug rerun shows SBI failures abort release for ~30% of UEs, so UE contexts and UDM SDM subscriptions are never released and the 4096 pool fills over repeated kills, rejecting registrations. AMF logs ERRORs at gNB loss (thread), and exhaustion needs many cycles/hundreds of UEs; not reproduced on 2.8.0.
MME does not send DDN Ack/Reject when implicit detach removes the UE context during paging (or after eNB ICS failure); UE unreachability, not an NF/peer failure event.

AMF fails to actually send NG Reset Acknowledge when the RAN node sends a (partial) NG Reset, so the reset procedure with the gNB never completes; maintainer fixed it. Visible as missing ack at the RAN/pcap; no evidence of persistent UE service failure.
Third-party SGW Create Session Request omitted the TEID field; thread: reporter confirmed the SGW was non-compliant. Interop/config issue, no failure event.

After gNB SCTP drop and reconnect, re-registering UEs get stale AMF/SMF state (thread: hypothesised zombie sess_list transplanted on SUCI re-attach; SMF did not release session on N1N2 400), so PDU session establishment fails every ~16 s with HTTP 400 and IPs leak; only restarting AMF/SMF recovers.

AMF assert(ran_ue) crash from stale ran_ue_id after an incomplete handover plus duplicate-IMSI registration, triggered when the Process-one gNBs are 'released'; unclear whether this gNB release is a peer failure/disconnect or the bug is just a handover/duplicate-IMSI path.

After request overload, the SMF stops answering on the established HTTP/2 connection; AMF SBI client (libcurl multiplexing) never tears down the half-dead connection, so every AMF->SMF request times out until process restart and PDU sessions fail. Killing the connection restores service immediately.
SMF does not send CHARGING_RELEASE to CHF when PDU session create fails in ApplySessionRules (empty PCF session rules); ordinary error-path leak, no NF/peer failure event.
Feature request to implement GTP Recovery counter/echo handling in SMF; not a bug report.

Crafted PFCP Session Establishment messages put the UPF in a bad state, leading SMF to see heartbeat loss and loop on re-association; the root defect is malformed/adversarial input handling (fuzzing territory), closed as duplicate.
'Unknown UE by 5G-S_TMSI' on registration; thread suggests wrong subscriber data (K/OPc); config/usage question.

SGW-U crashes with ogs_pool_alloc() failed (timer pool) and xact assert 15 s after heartbeat loss/de-association from a distant SGW-C after 5 days uptime; no replies, so unclear whether it is a re-association leak bug or resource sizing (reporter asks for parameters).
SIM appears unusable after a failed registration caused by a wrong OPc; config/UE-side problem, restart only mentioned in passing.
UPF ogs_tun_read() warnings and no internet after host reboot; ogstun/NAT setup problem, usage question.
UPF panics on a PFCP Association Setup Request missing the Recovery Time Stamp IE (nil deref); malformed-input crash, no peer failure (CVE).

After AMF pod restart with a new IP, SMF keeps a cached per-SMContext CommunicationClient and NRF/cache return stale AMF profiles, so N1N2MessageTransfer times out to the dead pod IP and PDU session establishment fails for all UEs (T3580 x5) until SMF restart.
AMF does not send Error Indication when gNB reuses an active RAN UE NGAP ID in a new INITIAL UE MESSAGE; protocol logical-error handling, no failure event.
UPF nil-deref crash on a PoC-sent PFCP Session Report Response for an already-deleted session; stale/malformed input crash without peer failure.
UE repeatedly does mobility registration updates; thread: resolved by DNS fix and lowering gNB MCS (RF/gNB config), some unrelated GUTI/NSSAI tweaks; no restart/peer-failure state bug.

After switching Amarisoft/Open5GS from SA to NSA/4G and back to SA, UE cannot be found and AMF gets SBI 504 errors; maintainer says some NF did not respond but thread unresolved, so failure event and bug-vs-config are unclear.

Mostly startup-order/config questions; one sub-issue: when a UPF (UPF-initiated association) is shut down, SMF does not select the remaining associated UPF and loops ('No UPFs are PFCP associated that are suited to RR'). Maintainer fixed RR selection, but the error also appeared with both UPFs up and the final fix was a config change, so restart-relatedness is unclear.

When the UPF does not answer a PFCP Session Deletion Request (peer unresponsive) and the AMF-side SBI stream is already gone, sess_5gc_timeout hits ogs_assert(stream) and aborts the SMF. The restarted SMF has lost its UE IP allocations, giving duplicate IPs and crash loops under churn. Root cause is an unguarded NULL on the peer-timeout path (other).

After an AMF restart it has lost the UE's NAS security context. The AMF then fails to decode the ciphered inner Registration Request (GUTI), and registration stops instead of falling back to authentication. The UE cannot re-register and the AMF logs a decode error.

After all CP NFs restart while the UPF keeps running, the SMF re-associates over PFCP but UE attach fails repeatedly: the UPF returns session-context errors and the CP stalls. Thread: maintainer reproduced it by restarting all NFs except the UPF, fixed it in main, and the reporter confirmed. Labelled stale-restoration because pre-restart UPF state conflicts after re-association; the exact mechanism is not stated.

GUTI/TMSI string-parsing bug and GUTI reuse in mobility registration update, plus a T3560 timer branch issue found with a NAS state-learning harness. Restarts are only per-trial resets, not a failure event.
SMF crash on attach. Thread: caused by a missing IPv6 subnet in the config while the UE/WebUI requested IPv4v6; fixed by a config change.
Security report: an unauthorized peer sends a PFCP Association Setup claiming an existing SMF Node ID and overwrites the association. Adversarial input, no peer failure/restart.

When the gNB restarts (new NG Setup), sends NG Reset or closes SCTP, release_ngap_context_only() moves UEs to CM-IDLE without starting the mobile reachable timer. A UE that never comes back therefore stays registered forever with no implicit deregistration. No error is shown, and in the test the UEs re-registered fine.
Security report: a rogue N2/SCTP association bursts InitialUEMessages and blocks the NGAP worker pool (DoS). Adversarial input, not a peer failure/restart state bug.
AMF/N3IWF/UPF use 100% CPU while SCTP is connected, due to the SCTP library (busy loop). Performance bug unrelated to a failure/restart event.

Repeated GTP-U Error Indications (peer reports lost state) for the same EPC bearer each start a separate deactivation. With no SGW-C responses, the duplicate PFCP remove makes the SMF hit ogs_assert(bearer) and abort. The bearer state tied to the peer event is mis-released: double removal, and the default bearer is removed leaving an empty session.

When the UPF stays associated but does not answer PFCP Session Deletion (timeout leads to SessionReleaseFailed), the duplicate-create path never releases the old SMContext. Each UE retry orphans one SMContext, its UE IP and its TEIDs, while the new session succeeds. Only a deletion retry-out WARN appears; the leak is internal and needs many retries to exhaust the pool.

After a UPF heartbeat failure is detected, the SMF's PFCP re-association never succeeds: Association Setup retries out repeatedly for 10+ minutes even though the UPF answers. Thread: the reporter traced it to the PFCP UDP receive goroutine blocking on the transaction EventChannel. Setup used an aggressive 10 ms heartbeat.

The UPF-adapter Association Setup Response handler drops UP Function Features, so the SMF never uses UPF-side UE IP allocation. This is a normal-path feature-negotiation bug with no failure/restart event.
SMF assertion in smf_sess_set_ue_ip when the UE connects with APN 'test2', which has no configured subnet. A config/usage problem with no peer failure.
gNB/eNB SCTP ABORT / connection refused. Thread: caused by the kernel SCTP module and wrong bind-address/interface configuration; resolved by config.

After an AMF reboot all UE contexts are lost. The AMF silently drops Service Requests from UEs that still think they are registered, instead of sending Service Reject #9, so the UEs retry forever and never reconnect. The AMF logs a state-mismatch error.
Suspected AmfUe leak in a release-command vs InitialUEMessage Service Request race. There is no peer failure. Thread: the maintainer explained the behavior is intended and the reporter agreed.

While the SMF is down or undiscoverable, the AMF registers a PDU session context, SMF selection fails, and the context is never removed. These survivors persist (copied on re-registration) and cost a 1 s timeout each on the single N1 thread at deregistration. The orphan state itself is not reported, and service recovers once the SMF is back.

After a UDR restart, the UDM still holds the released UDR nf_instance pointer in service_type_array (incomplete cleanup / reference count). It uses that client's default port 80, and UE re-registration fails with connection refused. Thread: maintainer fixed it by storing nf_instance_id and checking validity on recovery.

The MME restarts when a UE connects while the configured SGs (VLR) peer is unreachable. The peer is the MSC/VLR, which is outside the listed core NFs, and there is no clear cross-NF state issue. Thread: maintainer calls this expected behavior with no fix.
